review_candidates.title: Senior Leadership and Workforce Systems Advisor
review_candidates.description: Overview The Senior Leadership & Workforce Systems Advisor provides strategic technical leadership for strengthening health workforce governance, leadership, workforce management, digital HRH systems, evidence-informed decision-making, institutional capacity, organizational development, monitoring, learning, adaptive management, and sustainable transition of HRH systems across Ethiopia under the RISE and ACSCEND HRH activities. The project supports the Government of Ethiopia to strengthen Human Resources for Health (HRH) systems, particularly in underserved and fragile settings where shortages of competent health workers, limited institutional capacity, and weak regulatory systems continue to affect access to quality primary health care. Working through national institutions and decentralized implementation platforms, the project advances sustainable, country-led HRH reforms that improve workforce competency, performance, resilience, and health system effectiveness. The Advisor leads implementation of project thematic area focusing on Workforce, Leadership Management, Governance (LMG) and Regulation while ensuring close integration with workforce development interventions. Working closely with the Ministry of Health, Regional Health Bureaus, Woreda Health Offices, Primary Health Care Units (PHCUs), civil service institutions, higher education institutions, professional associations, and development partners, the Advisor strengthens the institutional systems required to plan, recruit, deploy, manage, develop, support, retain, and sustain a high-performing health workforce. The Advisor strengthens the institutional capacity of national and subnational HRH institutions to sustainably lead workforce governance, organizational development, leadership, digital transformation, and evidence-informed decision-making while promoting government ownership, adaptive management, organizational resilience, and long-term sustainability. The position ensures that all technical interventions reflect national priorities, international best practices, implementation science, digital innovation, and the America First Global Health Strategy (AFGHS) Position contingent on MOH and donor guidance. Responsibilities Strategic Technical Leadership Lead technical implementation of project thematic area focusing on LMG while providing strategic oversight for workforce systems interventions Develop long-term technical strategies, implementation frameworks, standards, implementation packages, operational guidance, and supportive supervision tools. Ensure technical interventions align with national HRH strategies, civil service reforms, emerging evidence, and global best practices. Lead annual technical planning, work planning, technical prioritization, and budgeting in collaboration with project leadership. Promote adaptive management through routine use of implementation data, stakeholder feedback, and implementation learning to continuously improve project performance. Lead institutional capacity strengthening initiatives that promote government ownership, sustainability, and transition of HRH systems to national and subnational institutions. Provide strategic leadership for innovation, organizational learning, implementation science, and continuous quality improvement across all workforce systems interventions. Leadership and Governance Strengthening Provide national technical leadership to strengthen leadership, governance, accountability, and organizational performance across the MoH, RHBs, WoHOs, PHCUs, and other supported institutions. Lead implementation of adaptive leadership, coaching, mentoring, succession planning, executive leadership development, leadership scorecards, governance systems, and continuous quality improvement initiatives. Strengthen organizational culture, accountability mechanisms, and performance management systems that improve leadership effectiveness. Strengthen leadership capacity for integrated primary health care management and service delivery. Promote learning organizations that foster innovation, teamwork, accountability, and adaptive leadership. Workforce Management Systems Provide strategic technical leadership for workforce planning, workforce budgeting, labor market analysis, workforce forecasting, recruitment, deployment, retention, workforce optimization, workload management, staff wellbeing, workforce continuity planning, and performance management. Strengthen institutionalization of evidence-based workforce planning approaches, including the Workload Indicators of Staffing Need (WISN), across PHCUs, WoHOs, RHBs, and national institutions. Strengthen implementation of HR policies, procedures, workforce governance, and human resource management systems. Support innovative workforce strategies, including Midwifery-Led Models of Care, nurse- and midwife-led clinics, rural workforce retention strategies, and other context-appropriate workforce optimization approaches. Strengthen workforce performance management systems, including leadership scorecards, Balanced Scorecard approaches where appropriate, and continuous organizational performance improvement. Promote workforce resilience and continuity planning to strengthen delivery of quality primary health care services. HRH Information Systems and Digital Transformation Lead implementation and institutionalization of woreda-based iHRIS, National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA), workforce intelligence systems, HRH dashboards, interoperability initiatives, and digital governance platforms. Strengthen national and subnational HRH digital architecture, interoperability, data quality, workforce analytics, and decision-support systems. Promote routine use of HRH information systems for evidence-informed planning, workforce optimization, monitoring, and policy decision-making. Provide technical leadership for digital innovation, artificial intelligence-supported HRH decision-making, and emerging technologies that improve workforce management. HRH Evidence, Research and Knowledge Management Promote evidence-informed implementation through implementation research, operational research, policy analysis, workforce analytics, and innovation. Strengthen HRH observatories, knowledge repositories, Communities of Practice, South-to-South learning initiatives, and innovation platforms. Support translation of research findings into national policy, program improvement, and workforce management practice. Promote organizational learning through systematic documentation and dissemination of best practices, innovations, lessons learned, policy briefs, technical reports, conference presentations, and peer-reviewed publications. Collaborate with national and international partners to advance innovation in HRH systems strengthening. Monitoring, Learning and Adaptive Management Provide strategic leadership to strengthen Monitoring, Evaluation, Research, Learning, and Adaptation (MERLA) systems that support continuous improvement of HRH interventions. Lead implementation of adaptive management approaches, implementation science, Collaborating, Learning, and Adapting (CLA), quality improvement, after-action reviews, performance reviews, action tracking, and accountability mechanisms. Promote implementation fidelity through routine supportive supervision, technical reviews, mentoring, coaching, and learning collaboratives. Strengthen routine use of monitoring data to support evidence-informed decision-making and organizational learning. Organizational Capacity and Transition Provide strategic leadership for organizational systems strengthening through OSCAR, organizational development, institutional capacity assessments, capacity development planning, and change management. Strengthen organizational capacity of national and subnational institutions to sustainably manage HRH systems and workforce reforms. review_candidates.title: Senior Cost Control & Project Recovery Manager
review_candidates.location: Abu Dhabi Emirate, United Arab Emirates
review_candidates.description: Senior Cost Control & Project Recovery Manager Are you a proven project recovery specialist with the ability to turn around underperforming EPC projects and deliver measurable commercial results? We are seeking a Senior Cost Control & Project Recovery Manager to lead cost governance, forecasting, and recovery initiatives on major Oil & Gas EPC projects. This is a strategic leadership role for an experienced professional who can move beyond traditional cost reporting and drive tangible improvements in project performance, productivity, and profitability. YOUR ROLE As Senior Cost Control & Project Recovery Manager , you will establish the project's true Cost-at-Completion (EAC) position and develop a robust, measurable recovery strategy to improve commercial outcomes. This role requires a hands-on leader who can identify cost leakage, challenge assumptions, determine root causes, quantify recovery opportunities, and influence senior project and construction teams to execute corrective actions. Project Cost Leadership Own and maintain the integrated cost control framework, including: Budget control, Actual costs, Commitments and accruals, Estimate to Complete (ETC), Estimate at Completion (EAC), Forecast margins, Cash flow interfaces Ensure alignment between WBS/CBS structures and project schedules, quantities, manpower, procurement, subcontracting, and area/commodity ownership. Productivity & Performance Analysis Measure earned versus actual man-hours and productivity across disciplines, areas, and commodities. Identify productivity losses, idle resources, and cost leakage. Analyze cost and schedule performance using objective project controls data. Project Recovery & Improvement Develop and maintain a quantified Project Recovery Plan covering: Productivity improvement, Workforce optimization, Demobilization strategies, Subcontract execution plans, Procurement and material exposure mitigation, Indirect cost reductions, Schedule acceleration and resequencing Track recovery initiatives through to realized savings and eliminate double-counting of benefits. Forecasting & Scenario Planning Forecast manpower and demobilization requirements based on remaining quantities and achievable productivity targets. Conduct scenario analysis on resource strategies, schedule outcomes, and recovery initiatives, demonstrating impacts on EAC and project profitability. Executive Reporting Deliver weekly and monthly variance analysis including: Root cause identification Accountable owners Corrective actions Financial impact assessment Target completion dates Develop executive-level dashboards using Excel, Power BI, and project source systems. Support management reviews with clear recommendations and proactive early warning indicators. Stakeholder Management Challenge Construction Managers and discipline leaders using factual cost, quantity, resource, and earned-hour data. Integrate cost performance with Primavera P6 schedules and commercial entitlement assessments. Distinguish recoverable client/EPC-caused costs from internal inefficiencies. WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR Experience Must have 15-20+ years of project controls and cost management experience. Significant experience within large-scale Oil & Gas EPC construction projects. Proven track record of successfully recovering or materially improving underperforming projects. Contractor-side EPC experience is essential. ADNOC, UAE, or broader GCC project experience is strongly preferred. Education and Certifications Bachelor’s Degree in any Specialization Skills and Competencies Advanced expertise in: Cost forecasting, Earned Value Management (EVM), Productivity and man-hour analysis, WBS/CBS development and integration, Commitments and accruals management, Cash flow forecasting Strong Primavera P6 knowledge. review_candidates.title: National Consultant - Assessment on Gender Statistics production, analysis, dissemination, and use at the national and regional level and identification of gaps
review_candidates.description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. Guided by the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, UN Women operates under a triple mandate—coordination, normative, and operational—which together define its unique role within the UN system. Through its coordination mandate, UN Women leads and harmonizes the UN system’s efforts to promote gender equality, ensuring coherence across agencies, programs, and country-level interventions. Its normative mandate focuses on supporting global standard setting by helping Member States develop, adopt, and monitor international norms and policies on gender equality and women’s rights, including contributing to processes such as the Commission on the Status of Women (CSW). Complementing these, the operational mandate enables UN Women to implement programs on the ground, working directly with governments, civil society, and communities to advance women’s empowerment, end gender-based violence, and promote economic and political participation. Together, these three dimensions reinforce UN Women’s comprehensive approach to driving transformative change for women and girls worldwide. UN Women is committed to eliminating discrimination against women and girls, empowering women, and achieving substantive equality between women and men across all spheres of development, human rights, humanitarian action, and peace and security. A central pillar of this mission is the strengthening of gender-responsive statistical systems that accurately reflect the lived realities and diverse experiences of all genders. Such systems are essential for evidence-based policymaking, effective program design, and institutional accountability. Traditional statistical systems often fail to capture gender-specific data and statistics, resulting in significant data gaps that obscure the lived experiences of women, men, girls, and boys. These gaps hinder the ability of policymakers and institutions to identify inequalities and design targeted, evidence-based interventions. Integrating gender perspectives across the entire statistical cycle including data collection, analysis, dissemination, and utilization enables the production of gender responsive, inclusive, reliable, and representative datasets. Beyond generating evidence, gender statistics serve as an essential resource for policymakers and legal drafters, illuminating the realities of women and men and informing the development of laws and policies that promote equity across all sectors such as health, education, agriculture, employment, and political participation and decision making. The Joint Programme “Strengthening Institutional Capacity of Gender Machineries in Ethiopia” implemented by UN Women and UNFPA Ethiopia Country Offices with financial support from the European Union and the Spanish Agency for International Development aims to strengthen gender mainstreaming systems, institutional capacity, gender statistics, coordination, and accountability mechanisms at the Federal and Regional level. One of the result areas for the joint programme is “strengthened mechanisms for Production, analysis and use gender-related data.’’ As part of this effort, a national assessment will be conducted to assess the current landscape of Ethiopia’s gender statistics system. The assessment will review existing initiatives, achievements, and institutional practices, while identifying persistent gaps and challenges. It will also examine how available gender statistics are utilized by policymakers and legal drafters to drive tangible improvements in the lives of women and vulnerable populations. To this end, UN Women is planning to bring on board a qualified national consultant to conduct a comprehensive assessment of the National statistics system and, analysis, dissemination, and use of gender statistics at both national and in Afar, Amhara, Tigray, Somali and Gambella regions. The consultant will work under the overall guidance and supervision of UN Women National Programme Coordinator and UNFPA Ethiopia Programme Specialist, in close collaboration with the Ministry of Women and Social Affairs Ethiopian Statistical Services (ESS) and relevant federal institutions. A technical task team may be established to provide guidance, review data collection tools, facilitate access to institutions and documents, and ensure quality assurance throughout the process. Description Of Responsibilities/ Scope Of Work The assessment will focus on the Federal Statistics Service and selected Regional Statistics Bureaus, with particular attention to selected pro-poor sectors at the federal and regional levels, including sectors such as, Ethiopian Statistics Service, Ministry of Women and Social Affairs, Ministry of Planning and Development, MOH, MOE, MOA, Ministry of skills and job creation, etc... and. The scope will examine how gender statistics are produced, analyzed, disseminated, and utilized within these institutions and sectors to inform inclusive development. In addition, the consulting firm will engage a broad range of stakeholders involved in policy formulation and legal drafting processes at both federal and regional levels (in Afar, Amhara, Tigray, Somali and Gambella regions), including relevant ministries, legislative bodies, and sectoral agencies, to assess how gender data informs decision-making and regulatory frameworks. The national consultant is expected to propose and justify the most appropriate and robust methodology for carrying out this assignment, combining qualitative and quantitative approaches as relevant, and ensuring participatory engagement with key stakeholders to generate comprehensive and actionable findings. Main Tasks And Responsibilities Conduct a comprehensive situational analysis of Ethiopia’s gender statistics system, including institutional frameworks, legal provisions, key stakeholders, and coordination mechanisms at national and in Afar, Amhara, Tigray, Somali and Gambella regions. Assess the production and quality of gender statistics by reviewing data sources, methodologies, standards compliance, and the availability of disaggregated data. Evaluate current systems for dissemination and accessibility of sex disaggregated data, and gender statistics, including platforms, communication tools, and user-friendliness for diverse audiences. Analyze how gender statistics are used by policymakers and legal drafters to inform policies, programs, and legislation, and identify barriers to effective utilization. Assess the technical and institutional capacities of relevant agencies involved in gender data production, analysis, management and utilization. Identify key gaps and challenges within the gender statistics ecosystem and develop practical, prioritized recommendations for improvement. Facilitate the collection of data at the regional level in Afar, Amhara, Gambella, Somali and Tigray regions including onboarding and managing data collectors Prepare and deliver key outputs, including an inception report, stakeholder consultations, validation of findings, and a comprehensive final assessment report. Deliverables The key deliverables for this assignment include: I. Inception Report: A detailed work plan outlining the assessment methodology, data collection tools, stakeholder engagement plan, and implementation schedule detailed work plan . II. Desk Review and Data Collection Summary report: A consolidated summary of reviewed documents, mapped data sources, and synthesized findings from field visits and stakeholder consultations. III. Draft Assessment Report: A draft report presenting preliminary findings on the production, dissemination, and use of gender statistics, including identified gaps and proposed recommendations. Validation Workshop Report: Documentation of stakeholder feedback, discussions, and agreed priority actions emerging from the validation workshop. V. Final Report on data gap on Gender Statistics: A comprehensive final report incorporating validated findings, actionable recommendations, and an executive summary with practical recommendations for key stakeholders including decision-makers. review_candidates.title: HR Generalist
review_candidates.description: Amref Health Africa, founded in 1957, is the largest African-based international health development organisation. Headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, Amref implements programmes across 35 African countries , reaching more than 40 million people , with a strong operational presence in Africa and advocacy and fundraising offices in Europe and North America. Guided by its vision of lasting health change in Africa , Amref’s mission is to catalyse community-led, people-centred health systems and address the social determinants of health . Amref believes sustainable health transformation is driven from within communities and works to strengthen health systems while empowering communities to demand and access quality, affordable healthcare. Job Description Please note that this is a short-term contract running until December 2026. JOB PURPOSE The HR Generalist supports the HR Business Partner, HQ in delivering reliable, responsive and employee-centred human resource services across the employee lifecycle. The role combines strong day-to-day people operations with future-focused HR practices by coordinating recruitment and onboarding, employee relations and experience, performance and talent processes, learning and future skills, workforce analytics, digital HR solutions and compliance. Through accurate service delivery, practical guidance, data-informed insights and continuous improvement, the role helps create an inclusive, agile and digitally enabled workplace while ensuring HR programmes and processes are implemented in line with organisational policies and applicable employment requirements. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES HR Operations, Employee Lifecycle and Service Delivery Coordinate employee lifecycle processes, including appointment, onboarding, probation and confirmation, contract changes and renewals, transfers, leave administration, separation and offboarding. Prepare accurate and timely employment documentation, employee correspondence and HR confirmations, and maintain trackers for contracts and other time-bound actions. Maintain complete, accurate and confidential employee records in the HR information system and personnel files, in line with data protection and records-management requirements. Support payroll and benefits administration by providing validated employee changes, completing routine reconciliations and resolving data discrepancies within agreed timelines. Provide first-line guidance to employees and managers on HR policies, processes and self-service tools, resolving routine queries and escalating complex or sensitive matters appropriately. Monitor recurring service queries and employee pain points and recommend practical improvements to the HR Business Partner. Talent Acquisition, Onboarding and Workforce Planning Support Support workforce planning by maintaining current headcount and vacancy information, tracking upcoming contract decisions and identifying emerging staffing or capability needs for review by the HR Business Partner. Coordinate recruitment processes from approved requisition through appointment, including job posting, application management, shortlisting administration, interview scheduling, candidate communication, pre-employment checks and appointment documentation. Support hiring managers to apply fair, inclusive and competency-based selection processes and maintain complete recruitment records in line with organisational policy. Coordinate onboarding and induction, including pre-boarding arrangements and scheduled follow-up, to help new employees integrate quickly and understand performance, culture, safeguarding and compliance expectations. Maintain recruitment and onboarding dashboards, monitor agreed timelines and candidate or new-joiner experience, and flag delays or improvement opportunities. Support development of talent pools for recurring and critical roles in line with approved workforce priorities. Employee Relations, Experience, Wellbeing and Culture Provide first-line support on routine employee relations matters, maintain accurate case records and refer complex, high-risk or sensitive cases to the HR Business Partner. Support fair and consistent implementation of employee relations processes, including attendance, conduct, grievance and performance-related matters, within established procedures. Coordinate employee listening, engagement, wellbeing and recognition initiatives; analyse feedback and track agreed actions with relevant leaders and teams. Gather feedback at key moments in the employee journey and use it to recommend improvements to employee experience and HR service delivery. Promote an inclusive, respectful and psychologically safe workplace by reinforcing organisational values, equity and inclusion, safeguarding expectations and relevant people policies. Performance, Talent, Learning and Future Skills Coordinate key stages of the performance management cycle, including goal setting, check-ins, review periods, documentation, completion tracking and follow-up with managers and employees. Support talent review, succession and employee development processes under the guidance of the HR Business Partner and relevant specialist teams. Coordinate learning-needs inputs and learning activities, including nominations, logistics, attendance, evaluation and maintenance of accurate training records. Track individual development plans, career-development actions and agreed learning commitments and provide completion and impact updates. Support initiatives that build future-relevant capabilities, including digital fluency, data literacy, collaboration, adaptability and people-management skills. People Analytics and Workforce Insights Maintain accurate workforce dashboards and trackers covering headcount, vacancies, contract status, recruitment, onboarding, turnover, absence, performance, learning and other agreed people indicators. Compile and analyse workforce data, identify patterns and emerging risks, and prepare concise reports and insights for the HR Business Partner and management decision-making. Support data quality checks, reconciliations and consistent use of workforce definitions across HR records, systems and reports. Translate employee and workforce data into practical follow-up actions and track whether agreed interventions deliver the intended improvement. HR Technology, Automation and Continuous Improvement Promote effective use of the HR information system, employee and manager self-service tools and approved digital workflows, and provide user guidance where required. Identify opportunities to simplify, standardise or automate repetitive HR processes while maintaining appropriate controls and a positive employee experience. Use approved digital and artificial intelligence-enabled tools responsibly to improve accuracy, insight and turnaround time, while ensuring data privacy, human oversight and compliance with organisational requirements. Maintain clear process maps, user guides and standard operating materials and support adoption of new HR tools and ways of working. Gather user feedback after process or technology changes and recommend refinements based on service data and employee experience. Policy, Risk, Governance and Change Support Support consistent application of organisational HR policies, procedures and internal controls and monitor completion of required documentation. Help ensure HR processes comply with applicable employment legislation, data protection, safeguarding and organisational requirements. Prepare documentation for internal and external audits, maintain agreed action trackers and support timely closure of HR findings and risks. Support people-related change initiatives through accurate employee data, coordinated communications, stakeholder follow-up and practical adoption support. Contribute operational insights to policy and process reviews and help communicate approved changes in clear and accessible language. Handle employee information with discretion and maintain strict confidentiality in all HR activities. Qualifications Academic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Human Resource Management, Business Administration or a related field. Professional Qualifications / Memberships Higher Diploma in Human Resource Management, CHRP qualification or an equivalent professional credential. Current membership of the Institute of Human Resource Management or another relevant professional body, as applicable. Experience Minimum of three (3) to five (5) years of relevant experience in an HR generalist or comparable role. Demonstrated experience supporting HR operations, recruitment and onboarding, employee relations, performance and learning processes, HR reporting and compliance in a diverse work environment. Practical experience using an HR information system and workforce data to support service delivery and decision-making. Exposure to HR digitalisation, process improvement, employee-experience or organisational-change initiatives is an advantage. Knowledge, Skills and Competencies Sound knowledge of end-to-end HR operations, employee lifecycle processes and contemporary people practices. Working knowledge of Kenyan employment legislation, HR compliance, governance, data protection and safeguarding requirements. Ability to provide responsive, accurate and practical HR support while maintaining a strong employee and manager service orientation. Strong employee-relations judgement, including the ability to recognise risk, maintain accurate records and escalate matters appropriately. Strong planning, project-coordination and organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver within agreed timelines. Strong interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills and the ability to build effective working relationships across teams and levels. Analytical capability, including the ability to interpret workforce data, identify trends and present clear, decision-relevant insights. Digital literacy and proficiency in HR information systems, Microsoft Office applications, reporting tools and employee self-service platforms. Curiosity and confidence to learn and responsibly apply emerging HR technologies, automation and artificial intelligence-enabled tools. Process-improvement mindset, with the ability to identify inefficiencies, propose practical solutions and support adoption of new ways of working. Adaptability and change orientation, with an interest in future workforce capabilities and evolving employee expectations. Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with professionalism, discretion and integrity. Commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, safeguarding, wellbeing and a positive employee experience. Collaborative, accountable and service-oriented approach, with a commitment to continuous learning and high-quality delivery. Additional Information Please submit your CV or resume highlighting relevant skills and experience along with a cover letter detailing why you are the best fit for this position. Kindly note that the application deadline is September 09, 2026 at 23:59 EAT. Amref Health Africa does not require applicants to pay any money at whatever stage of the recruitment and selection process and has not retained any agent in connection with recruitment. Although Amref may use different job boards from time to time to further spread its reach for applicants, all open vacancies are published on our website under the Vacancies page and on our official social media pages. Kindly also note that official emails from Amref Health Africa will arrive from an @amref.org address. Amref Health Africa is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all staff to share this commitment. Amref Health Africa is is dedicated to diversity and is an equal-opportunity employer with a non-smoking environment policy.

In its pursuit to excel as a hybrid luxury retailer, the Group has curated a portfolio of over 10 owned brands and strengthened its distribution and marketing expertise for over 400 international names across luxury fashion, beauty, jewellery, watches, eyewear, and art de vivre categories. Driving this innovation journey is The Greenhouse — the Group’s innovation hub, incubator, and accelerator for startups and emerging businesses, regionally and globally. Chalhoub Group fosters a people-at-heart culture rooted in diversity, equity, and inclusion, and a workplace catalysed by forward thinking and future-proofing. Today, it brings together over 16,000 talented professionals across eight countries in the Middle East, with a presence in LATAM. Sustainability is at the core of the Group’s strategy, guided by a clear commitment to people, partners, and the planet. Chalhoub Group is proud to be a member of the United Nations Global Compact, a signatory of the Women’s Empowerment Principles, and to have pledged to reach Net Zero by 2040. What You'll Be Doing The People Experience & Culture Specialist leads the localisation and activation of the Group’s culture, employee experience, engagement, and wellbeing agenda in Egypt. Working closely with the Egypt leadership team, People Partners, and Group People Experience & Culture, the role translates Group priorities and employee insights into relevant country-level strategies and interventions. It provides specialist expertise to leaders, shapes key moments across the employee journey, and leads initiatives that strengthen engagement, inclusion, wellbeing, and the overall workplace experience. The role also positions Egypt as a test-and-learn market by designing and piloting new approaches, measuring their impact, and sharing insights and effective practices with the wider Group. What You’ll Need To Succeed Country People Experience and Culture Strategy Co-create and drive the Egypt People Experience & Culture roadmap with the country leadership team, ensuring alignment with Group priorities and local business and workforce needs. Translate employee and business insights into targeted priorities, interventions, and action plans. Partner with leaders to strengthen team cultures and embed inclusive, engaging, and healthy ways of working. Monitor the progress and impact of the country roadmap, identifying risks, gaps, and opportunities for continuous improvement. Culture Activation and Change Lead the country activation and embedding of the Group’s culture principles and behaviours, adapting initiatives to ensure local relevance while maintaining their intended purpose. Design and facilitate culture interventions, including bootcamps, culture labs, hackathons, leadership sessions, and co-creation forums. Partner with leaders and People Partners to diagnose and address culture priorities at country, business-unit, and team levels. Build accountability and advocacy for culture across leadership teams, employee communities, and local champions. Design and deliver people centred change and communication campaigns that build understanding, participation, and sustained behaviour change. Mobilise People Experience & Culture communities and employee champions to strengthen bottom-up ownership of the workplace experience. Employee Listening, Engagement and Wellbeing Lead the Voice of People survey and other employee-listening activities in Egypt, including pulse checks, interviews, focus groups, and workshops. Partner with leaders and People Partners to interpret findings, identify priority areas, and translate insights into measurable action plans. Lead the Great Place to Work certification process in Egypt, coordinating stakeholders, communications, submissions, and follow-up actions. Design and deliver engagement and wellbeing initiatives that respond to employee needs and support a healthy, inclusive, and connected workplace. Facilitate employee forums, town halls, listening sessions, and events that promote dialogue, transparency, and connection. Support internal and external storytelling that strengthens employee engagement and showcases the workplace experience in Egypt. Employee Journey And Experience Design Lead employee journey mapping exercises across priority stages of the employee lifecycle to identify experience gaps and improvement opportunities. Partner with business units and People Partners to conduct employee experience diagnostics using quantitative and qualitative research methods. Facilitate design thinking and co-creation workshops to redesign priority experiences from an employee centred perspective. Localise and deploy Group employee experience products and solutions, including onboarding, internal mobility, flexible working, and other priority touchpoints. Design and pilot new employee experience interventions in Egypt, evaluate their effectiveness, and recommend opportunities for wider implementation. Insights, Analytics and Impact Consolidate and analyse employee experience, culture, engagement, and wellbeing data to identify trends, risks, and improvement opportunities. Develop reports, dashboards, and executive presentations that translate data into meaningful insights and recommendations for leaders and the People & Culture community. Establish relevant success measures for initiatives and evaluate their reach, effectiveness, adoption, and employee impact. Integrate insights from different listening channels to provide a holistic view of the employee experience in Egypt. Strategic Advisory and Stakeholder Partnership Build trusted relationships with senior leaders, People Partners, and key stakeholders to understand priorities and elevate culture and employee experience across Egypt. Act as a trusted advisor on culture, employee experience, engagement, and wellbeing, offering insight-led recommendations and constructively challenging leaders where needed. Partner with leaders to diagnose needs, co-create relevant interventions, and translate priorities into sustainable action. Connect country and Group stakeholders to strengthen alignment, share effective practices, and maintain collective ownership of outcomes What We Can Offer You With us, you will turn your aspirations into reality. We will help shape your journey through enriching experiences, learning and development opportunities and exposure to different assignments within your role or through internal mobility. We ensure equal opportunity for all our applicants without regard to gender, age, race, religion, national origin or disability status.

new_matches.description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. Guided by the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, UN Women operates under a triple mandate—coordination, normative, and operational—which together define its unique role within the UN system. Through its coordination mandate, UN Women leads and harmonizes the UN system’s efforts to promote gender equality, ensuring coherence across agencies, programs, and country-level interventions. Its normative mandate focuses on supporting global standard setting by helping Member States develop, adopt, and monitor international norms and policies on gender equality and women’s rights, including contributing to processes such as the Commission on the Status of Women (CSW). Complementing these, the operational mandate enables UN Women to implement programs on the ground, working directly with governments, civil society, and communities to advance women’s empowerment, end gender-based violence, and promote economic and political participation. Together, these three dimensions reinforce UN Women’s comprehensive approach to driving transformative change for women and girls worldwide. UN Women is committed to eliminating discrimination against women and girls, empowering women, and achieving substantive equality between women and men across all spheres of development, human rights, humanitarian action, and peace and security. A central pillar of this mission is the strengthening of gender-responsive statistical systems that accurately reflect the lived realities and diverse experiences of all genders. Such systems are essential for evidence-based policymaking, effective program design, and institutional accountability. Traditional statistical systems often fail to capture gender-specific data and statistics, resulting in significant data gaps that obscure the lived experiences of women, men, girls, and boys. These gaps hinder the ability of policymakers and institutions to identify inequalities and design targeted, evidence-based interventions. Integrating gender perspectives across the entire statistical cycle including data collection, analysis, dissemination, and utilization enables the production of gender responsive, inclusive, reliable, and representative datasets. Beyond generating evidence, gender statistics serve as an essential resource for policymakers and legal drafters, illuminating the realities of women and men and informing the development of laws and policies that promote equity across all sectors such as health, education, agriculture, employment, and political participation and decision making. The Joint Programme “Strengthening Institutional Capacity of Gender Machineries in Ethiopia” implemented by UN Women and UNFPA Ethiopia Country Offices with financial support from the European Union and the Spanish Agency for International Development aims to strengthen gender mainstreaming systems, institutional capacity, gender statistics, coordination, and accountability mechanisms at the Federal and Regional level. One of the result areas for the joint programme is “strengthened mechanisms for Production, analysis and use gender-related data.’’ As part of this effort, a national assessment will be conducted to assess the current landscape of Ethiopia’s gender statistics system. The assessment will review existing initiatives, achievements, and institutional practices, while identifying persistent gaps and challenges. It will also examine how available gender statistics are utilized by policymakers and legal drafters to drive tangible improvements in the lives of women and vulnerable populations. To this end, UN Women is planning to bring on board a qualified national consultant to conduct a comprehensive assessment of the National statistics system and, analysis, dissemination, and use of gender statistics at both national and in Afar, Amhara, Tigray, Somali and Gambella regions. The consultant will work under the overall guidance and supervision of UN Women National Programme Coordinator and UNFPA Ethiopia Programme Specialist, in close collaboration with the Ministry of Women and Social Affairs Ethiopian Statistical Services (ESS) and relevant federal institutions. A technical task team may be established to provide guidance, review data collection tools, facilitate access to institutions and documents, and ensure quality assurance throughout the process. Description Of Responsibilities/ Scope Of Work The assessment will focus on the Federal Statistics Service and selected Regional Statistics Bureaus, with particular attention to selected pro-poor sectors at the federal and regional levels, including sectors such as, Ethiopian Statistics Service, Ministry of Women and Social Affairs, Ministry of Planning and Development, MOH, MOE, MOA, Ministry of skills and job creation, etc... and. The scope will examine how gender statistics are produced, analyzed, disseminated, and utilized within these institutions and sectors to inform inclusive development. In addition, the consulting firm will engage a broad range of stakeholders involved in policy formulation and legal drafting processes at both federal and regional levels (in Afar, Amhara, Tigray, Somali and Gambella regions), including relevant ministries, legislative bodies, and sectoral agencies, to assess how gender data informs decision-making and regulatory frameworks. The national consultant is expected to propose and justify the most appropriate and robust methodology for carrying out this assignment, combining qualitative and quantitative approaches as relevant, and ensuring participatory engagement with key stakeholders to generate comprehensive and actionable findings. Main Tasks And Responsibilities Conduct a comprehensive situational analysis of Ethiopia’s gender statistics system, including institutional frameworks, legal provisions, key stakeholders, and coordination mechanisms at national and in Afar, Amhara, Tigray, Somali and Gambella regions. Assess the production and quality of gender statistics by reviewing data sources, methodologies, standards compliance, and the availability of disaggregated data. Evaluate current systems for dissemination and accessibility of sex disaggregated data, and gender statistics, including platforms, communication tools, and user-friendliness for diverse audiences. Analyze how gender statistics are used by policymakers and legal drafters to inform policies, programs, and legislation, and identify barriers to effective utilization. Assess the technical and institutional capacities of relevant agencies involved in gender data production, analysis, management and utilization. Identify key gaps and challenges within the gender statistics ecosystem and develop practical, prioritized recommendations for improvement. Facilitate the collection of data at the regional level in Afar, Amhara, Gambella, Somali and Tigray regions including onboarding and managing data collectors Prepare and deliver key outputs, including an inception report, stakeholder consultations, validation of findings, and a comprehensive final assessment report. Deliverables The key deliverables for this assignment include: I. Inception Report: A detailed work plan outlining the assessment methodology, data collection tools, stakeholder engagement plan, and implementation schedule detailed work plan . II. Desk Review and Data Collection Summary report: A consolidated summary of reviewed documents, mapped data sources, and synthesized findings from field visits and stakeholder consultations. III. Draft Assessment Report: A draft report presenting preliminary findings on the production, dissemination, and use of gender statistics, including identified gaps and proposed recommendations. Validation Workshop Report: Documentation of stakeholder feedback, discussions, and agreed priority actions emerging from the validation workshop. V. Final Report on data gap on Gender Statistics: A comprehensive final report incorporating validated findings, actionable recommendations, and an executive summary with practical recommendations for key stakeholders including decision-makers. Through strategic, high-quality design across print and digital platforms, the global designer supports programmatic, fundraising, partnerships, advocacy, and global marketing and communication efforts. The ideal candidate brings strong layout and typography skills, the ability to translate complex ideas into clear, compelling visual communications, a flexible and collaborative mindset, and the ability to track and manage multiple work streams. With guidance from the Art Manager and Senior Manager of Global Communications, the designer collaborates across multiple site teams (working closely with the Site Communications Leads) to create a wide range of materials and supports in upholding global brand alignment. Responsibilities And Deliverables Creative Execution (90%) Design compelling print and digital visual materials that engage diverse audiences—including patients, staff, high-impact donors, and prospective supporters—while supporting site-specific priorities. Key projects may include newsletters, annual and impact reports, social media posts, brochures, one-pagers, posters, presentations, and internal documents, among others. Work closely with the Senior Manager of Global Communications to manage multiple concurrent projects across three site teams, prioritize competing deadlines, and proactively adjust workload to meet shifting organizational needs. Create clear and engaging illustrations, dashboards, infographics, graphs, and charts for both academic and general audiences. Design high-quality deliverables for events including visual branding, digital promotion, and exhibition materials. Ensure brand and messaging consistency across all visual communications by applying established visual guidelines across all physical and digital materials. Design Support (10%) Collaborate and communicate effectively across cultures, departments, and time zones by clearly articulating design choices, actively listening to feedback, and building strong working relationships. Work closely with the Art Manager as well as Site Communications Leads, writers, multimedia, and programmatic teams to create high-quality deliverables that are on-brand , on deadline, on budget, and meet stated goals. Support the growth of a shared design system by creating templates, guidelines, and assets for other global designers and non-designer colleagues. Participate in brainstorming sessions and contribute ideas for visual storytelling, campaigns, and audience-specific experiences. Stay up-to-date on accessibility standards and design best practices to ensure copy and visuals are legible and accessible to diverse audiences. Work with Site Procurement teams to communicate with external printers and merch vendors as needed. Conduct bi-annual basic trainings on graphic design principles and techniques for interested local comms staff to help support this function globally. Qualifications, Experience And Skills Bachelor's Degree in Graphic Design, Visual Communication, Fine Arts, Multimedia Design, Communications Design, or a related field. At least 5 years' professional experience in graphic design or a related field. Strong portfolio demonstrating a broad range of professional print and digital design work, including strong skills in layout, branding, and typography. Proficiency with Adobe Creative Cloud, specifically InDesign, Illustrator, and Photoshop. Familiarity with Canva , Figma , or similar design tools. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent deadlines across different stakeholders while delivering quality work on time and within budget. Excellent and exemplary interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with culturally diverse staff across departments and countries. Experience working on design projects for nonprofit, international development, health, or other mission-driven organizations will be an added advantage. Experience in illustration, infographic development, or data visualization will be an added advantage. CORE VALUES AND COMPETENCIES Demonstrates the organization’s core values of: Commitment, Humility, Integrity, and Pragmatic Solidarity/Accompaniment. Accountability – Able to accept responsibility for one's actions and outcomes, plus those of their team. Achieving results – Able to set realistic goals, put plans into action, monitor progress, evaluate outcomes, and apply lessons learned. Adaptability – Able to adapt to change, balance multiple demands, consider new approaches, and persist towards solutions in changing circumstances. Teamwork – Able to work well with others to achieve common goals. Exemplary interpersonal skills; ability to collaborate effectively with staff across departments and countries. Cultural sensitivity and flexibility. METHOD OF APPLICATION All interested and qualified candidates based in Malawi should apply strictly through https://www.pih.org/employment on or before 13 th September 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be invited for interviews. new_matches.title: Cost Control Manager
new_matches.description: We are looking for a Cost Control Manager to lead and manage all project cost control functions throughout the project lifecycle. The role is responsible for budgeting, cost monitoring, forecasting, invoicing, variation order assessments, and commercial reporting while working closely with project management, planning, contracts, procurement, and site teams to ensure projects are delivered within approved budgets and contractual requirements. Key Responsibilities: 1. Cost Planning and Budget Management Develop, monitor, and control project budgets, cost plans, and cash flow forecasts. Track project expenditures against approved budgets and identify cost variances. Prepare regular cost reports and provide recommendations to improve project profitability. Support project teams in achieving cost efficiency throughout project execution. 2. Cost Monitoring and Performance Control Monitor project costs, commitments, and earned value to ensure financial performance. Analyze cost trends and identify potential risks affecting project budgets. Prepare cost forecasts and final cost estimates for management review. Ensure compliance with company cost control procedures and reporting standards. 3. Invoicing and Payment Management Review, verify, and prepare client progress invoices in accordance with contract requirements. Monitor invoice status, certifications, and collections. Review subcontractor and supplier payment applications against completed work and contractual terms. Coordinate with Finance and Project Management to ensure accurate billing and payment processes. 4. Variation Orders and Commercial Management Lead the preparation, assessment, pricing, and negotiation of variation orders. Evaluate change requests and assess their financial impact on project budgets. Coordinate with Contracts, Project Managers, and Quantity Surveyors to prepare supporting documentation. Monitor approved and pending variations to ensure timely submission and recovery. 5. Contracts and Project Controls Coordination Work closely with Contracts, Planning, Procurement, and Project teams to ensure alignment between cost, schedule, and contractual obligations. Review contract provisions related to payments, claims, and cost recovery. Support commercial evaluations and contractual compliance throughout the project lifecycle. 6. Reporting and Financial Analysis Prepare periodic cost reports and financial dashboards. Monitor project cost performance, forecasting, and profitability. Recommend corrective actions to improve budget performance. 7. Team Leadership and Continuous Improvement Lead and support the Cost Control team. Improve cost control processes and reporting systems. Coordinate with project, commercial, planning, procurement, and finance teams. Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in civil engineering. Minimum 10+ years of experience in cost control, project controls, or commercial management within building construction projects. Previous experience managing cost control teams is highly preferred. Technical Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Required: Strong knowledge of construction cost control principles, budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting. Proven experience in invoicing, interim payment applications, variation order assessments, and cost analysis. Strong understanding of construction contracts, commercial management, and project controls. Experience working closely with Project Managers, Quantity Surveyors, Planning Engineers, and Contracts teams. Proficiency in MS Excel (Advanced), MS Office, and project control software (Primavera P6 knowledge is an advantage). Excellent analytical, financial, and problem-solving skills. Strong negotiation, communication, and stakeholder management abilities. Ability to manage multiple projects while maintaining accuracy under tight deadlines.
